# Heisenberg path representation and extensive Gaussian log coefficients

Author checkpoint, 6 October 2026. Base BGS
f285ba510732edd9ee3679b12316df9b12e0dfcb. No canonical or remote edits.
The results below are (A) an actual uniform trace representation with an
operator-controlled remainder, and (B) a rigorous FORMAL connected-Gaussian
coefficient theorem. They are not a uniform stationary-phase remainder
theorem, not an orbitwise trace formula at m~N, and not TRACE-005.

## 1. Exact target and two different remainders

Keep U_N=exp(i tau N A_N)M_N, tau=10^-80, all odd N. Fix b<infinity and
w in C_c^infinity((0,b)). The pair target is the complete signed sum
N^-2 sum_m w(m/N)(|Tr U_N^m|²-min(m,N)) ->0. The stable band b<1/2
is a necessary subtarget with min(m,N)=m.

The one-step WKB remainder and a later orbitwise stationary-phase remainder
are DIFFERENT. The first is controlled without summing absolute path or
branch weights. The second, if obtained only relatively per saddle, faces
exponential absolute orbit mass. Sections 2 and 7 keep these separate.

## 2. Actual uniform finite-path representation

Continue the exact transport recursion in four_branch_parametrix.md to
amplitudes a_(r,0),...,a_(r,J), for any FIXED integer J>=1. Put

V_N(j,k)=e(3N/8)/(2 sqrt(N)) sum_(r=0)^3
 e(N S_r(tau,j/N,k/N)) sum_(ell=0)^J N^-ell a_(r,ell)(tau,j/N,k/N).

The same finite Taylor/Duhamel proof as the published two-amplitude case
has factored residual O(N^-(J+1)), entrywise residual O(N^-(J+3/2)),
and hence operator residual O(N^-(J+1/2)). Initial higher amplitudes are
zero, so integration over the fixed time gives

delta_N:=||U_N-V_N||op <= C_J N^-(J+1/2).                 (A1)

This uses arbitrarily high but FIXED transport order, not a convergent
infinite symbol and not a long-time Egorov estimate. The gluing identities
persist under the recursion by uniqueness, as in the published proof.

Since ||V_N||<=1+delta_N, exact telescoping gives, for every m>=1,

||U_N^m-V_N^m|| <=m delta_N(1+delta_N)^(m-1),
|Tr U_N^m-Tr V_N^m| <=N m delta_N exp(m delta_N).         (A2)

Thus uniformly for 1<=m<=bN the trace error is O_(J,b)(N^(3/2-J)).
There is NO factor 4^m. The factor N in (A2) is the ordinary trace bound;
it is not omitted or replaced by a normalized trace.

The trace of V_N^m is EXACTLY

e(3mN/8) (2 sqrt(N))^-m
 sum_(x in (Z/N)^m) sum_(r in {0,1,2,3}^m)
 e(N sum_j S_(r_j)(tau,x_j/N,x_(j+1)/N))
 product_j [sum_(ell=0)^J N^-ell a_(r_j,ell)(tau,x_j/N,x_(j+1)/N)],

with x_m=x_0. This is a finite signed representation, including all
branches and all coordinate paths. It is not yet an integral over saddles.

If epsilon_N is the uniform trace error in (A2), |Tr U_N^m|<=N implies

N^-2 sum_(1<=m<=bN) |w(m/N)|
 | |Tr U_N^m|²-|Tr V_N^m|² |
 <= C_(w,b) (2 epsilon_N+epsilon_N²/N).               (A3)

For J>=2 this tends to zero; J can be increased to give any fixed
polynomial accuracy. Equation (A3) permits taking the modulus outside
the COMPLETE target sum and bounds only the controlled replacement error.
It says nothing about cancellation within the displayed finite path sum.

## 3. Actual Hessians: uniform mass and inverse decay

For a fixed lifted branch/winding class let
Phi(x)=sum_j S_(r_j)(tau,x_j,x_(j+1)) plus its linear alias terms.
The cyclic Hessian at any real x is nearest-neighbour. At zero coupling,

v^T H_0 v=-(3/2)sum v_j²+(1/2)sum v_j v_(j+1),
so -2I<=H_0<=-I.

The actual specified-time C² bounds give each one-step Hessian entry an
error at most epsilon=10^10 tau+10^50 tau²<2*10^-70. Summing the local
quadratic forms gives ||H-H_0||<=4epsilon, independently of m. All linear
alias/gluing terms leave this unchanged. Repeated neighbours at m=1,2
are counted by this quadratic-form formula, not by an incorrect simple
cycle convention.

Set K=-H. For m>=2 write K=D-R with D diagonal. Uniformly,
D_jj>=7/5 and sum_k |R_jk|<=3/5. Therefore rho=3/7 bounds
||D^-1 R||_infinity. The Neumann series and finite propagation on the
cycle give

sum_k |(K^-1)_(jk)|<=5/4,
|(K^-1)_(jk)| <=(5/4)(3/7)^(d_m(j,k)),                 (B1)

where d_m is cyclic graph distance. At m=1, K>=1-4epsilon>4/5 and
(B1) is immediate. These statements hold at EVERY real stationary class,
not just at a selected orbit. No assumption of absence of orbit clusters
is involved.

In stationary-phase normalization h=(2pi N)^-1, the formal Gaussian
covariance for exp(-i y^T K y/2) is C=-i K^-1. Its absolute row sums obey
the same bound. This is a Fresnel/Wick functional, not a positive measure.

## 4. Uniform local analyticity and the formal object

At fixed tau the one-step HJ solution and every fixed finite set of
transport amplitudes are real analytic, with a common small complex
neighbourhood and bounds independent of the real chart after gluing.
This follows directly from the finite Fourier symbol, the short fixed-time
holomorphic characteristic flow, and its uniformly invertible projection.
Compactness of the finitely many fundamental charts gives common constants.
The leading transport amplitude is nonzero (indeed close to 1); for each
fixed J and small h the finite amplitude polynomial is nonzero on a smaller
common complex neighbourhood. Its logarithm is therefore analytic there.
No analytic-in-J bound is being inferred from fixed-J transport existence.

Expand about any real stationary point x*. Put x=x*+sqrt(h)y, factor
out the phase, its quadratic Gaussian and the leading saddle amplitude.
The remaining exponent is a SUM of local vertices, one for each edge:

- phase vertices of polynomial degree d>=3 carry h^((d-2)/2);
- log-amplitude vertices of degree d>=0 and symbol order s>=0 carry
  h^(s+d/2), with s+d/2>0 after removing the constant leading term.

Every vertex depends on at most (y_j,y_(j+1)). Local analytic Taylor
coefficients are bounded by M R^-(d+s), with fixed M,R>0 independent of
m, the stationary class, and j (constants may depend on fixed J and tau).
The finite-J amplitude polynomial has a local analytic logarithm in h,
so these bounds include its induced infinite formal log series in h.

Let Z_m(h) be the FORMAL Gaussian expectation of the exponential of these
vertices, and write

log Z_m(h)=sum_(k>=1) ell_(k,m) h^k.                   (B2)

Odd half-powers vanish: the total Gaussian degree and the total half-power
grade have the same parity. Equation (B2) is a definition by Wick
contraction of finite polynomials at each order. No convergence of Z or
its logarithm is asserted.

## 5. The constructive coefficient theorem

There is C<infinity, depending only on the above local bounds and not on
m or the stationary class, such that

|ell_(k,m)| <= m C^k k! for every k>=1.                (B3)

PROOF. The formal exponential/logarithm identity expresses ell_k as the
sum of CONNECTED Wick diagrams. This can be proved without probabilistic
input: partition each Wick pairing into its connected components on the
vertex labels, and apply the exponential formula for labelled sets.
The exponential carries 1/r! for r vertices. Self-contractions are allowed.

At order h^k the total half-power grade is 2k. Each nonconstant vertex
has grade at least one, hence r<=2k. If D is total polynomial degree,
phase vertices add two more legs than their grade, while amplitude
vertices add at most their grade. Consequently

D<=2k+2r<=6k; write D=2E, so E<=k+r.

For a connected diagram with r>=2, choose any spanning tree of its
cross-vertex contraction graph by a fixed deterministic rule. For each
fixed choice of which of the two local coordinates each leg uses, sum
site labels from the leaves of this tree. Every removed leaf costs at
most sum_k |C_(a,k+sigma)|<=5/4. Every non-tree covariance costs at most
5/4 as well. The remaining root label has m choices. Thus the ENTIRE
site-label sum for each connected Wick diagram is bounded by

m (5/4)^E,

rather than m^r. This bound does not enumerate spanning trees, so it
introduces no additional r^(r-2) combinatorial loss. A deterministic
spanning tree is selected only to bound each already-counted pairing.
For r=1 the same bound is direct. Degree-zero vertices cannot belong to
a connected diagram with r>=2; their r=1 contributions are bounded separately
by m C^k.

The number of pairings of D=2E labelled legs is
(2E-1)!! <=2^E E!. After the exponential denominator 1/r!,

(2E-1)!!/r! <=2^(k+r)(3k)^k <=C_1^k k!.

If E<r, use E!/r!<=1; otherwise the ratio has at most k factors, each
at most 3k. The last inequality follows from k^k<=e^k k!.

There are only exponentially many ordered grade/type choices at fixed
2k: compositions of 2k contribute at most 2^(2k); choices of phase versus
amplitude and of symbol order/degree contribute another C_2^k. Expanding
a two-variable degree-d local polynomial gives at most d+1<=2^d monomial
choices. Their product and the analytic coefficient bounds contribute
C_3^k because D<=6k, r<=2k and total symbol order <=k. Collecting the
bounds proves (B3). END PROOF.

This theorem establishes dimension-uniform Gevrey-1 FORMAL log coefficients.
In particular ell_1=O(m), and at m~N its contribution h ell_1 is O(1).
For fixed k>=2, h^k ell_k=O(N^(1-k)). Thus resumming the first extensive
correction is structurally appropriate. The theorem does not justify
truncating the infinite formal series or identify it with an actual integral.

## 6. Executed connected-cancellation check

For the exactly solvable cyclic Hessian K_0 and the homogeneous toy phase

-x^T K_0 x/2 + u sum_j x_j³/6 + v sum_j x_j⁴/24,

write G=K_0^-1 and g_r=G_(0r). The first log coefficient is exactly

ell_1=-i m [(v+u²)g_0²/8 + u² sum_r g_r³/12].         (B4)

Wick's rule gives E(y_i³y_j³)=9 C_ii C_jj C_ij+6 C_ij³,
and sum_j G_ij=1. For u=v=1 the bracket tends to 13/84 as m->infinity.
This is a check of the uniform local resummation, not the claim that the
actual model's cubic and quartic jets are constant.

For a quartic-only test, the second connected moment is exactly

cum_2(sum_j y_j⁴)=m[72 g_0² sum_r g_r²+24 sum_r g_r⁴]

for the positive real Gaussian G. The disconnected 9m²g_0⁴ term cancels
from the logarithm. This explicitly checks the mechanism that removes
spurious dimension-squared growth.

cluster_checks.py verifies these identities, row sums and decay bounds
with exact rational matrices at m=1,...,18, and the factorial estimate in
(B3) for all k<=25, r<=2k and E<=k+r. The infinite-m value in (B4) is
symbolically reduced from g_r=(1/sqrt(2))(3-2sqrt(2))^|r| to 13/84.
These are exact finite/combinatorial checks, not an analytic remainder test.

## 7. First unresolved analytic step and the separate entropy loss

(B3) is insufficient to conclude an actual remainder bound. Needed next is
a volume-uniform contour/localization and zero-free logarithm theorem that
identifies the original oscillatory integral with the Gaussian local
expansion and controls its optimally truncated remainder. A formal Gevrey
bound alone does not supply such a theorem.

Rotating a local Gaussian contour by exp(-i pi/4) gives positive covariance
G. In a small complex neighbourhood the nonlinear real part is dominated
by the massive quadratic form, suggesting a local analytic cluster theorem.
But arbitrary real chart cutoffs are not analytic. Rotating each bounded
real chart separately produces side contours; their cancellation across
branch and winding boundaries must be proved. Neither the one-step gluing
identities nor (B3) alone proves that global contour statement. This is the
first remaining implication, before any orbit-counting estimate.

Even suppose a valid per-class expansion gave relative remainder e^-cN.
Summing it ABSOLUTELY over stationary classes is a second loss. For the
usual leading stability weights b_gamma=|det(I-DG^m)|^-1/2, the actual
bounds used in FM-007 give, for m>=2,

#Fix(G^m)<=6^m,  |det(I-DG^m)|>=4^m,
so sum_gamma b_gamma<=3^m.                              (B5)

The lower determinant bound follows from DG>=B, B=[[5/2,7/2],[3/2,5/2]],
det B=1 and its larger eigenvalue >4; Tr(B^m)-2>=4^m for m>=2.
The fixed-point count is the exact covering degree |det(S^m-I)|.
These classical statements do not assert a quantum trace formula.

Consequently a relative e^-cN error gives at best
O(exp[(b log 3-c)N]) for m<=bN, apart from polynomial and bounded
resummed-amplitude factors. This establishes decay only when
b<c/log 3. It does not cover arbitrary compact Heisenberg bands with one
fixed exponent c. Fixed algebraic per-orbit errors do not overcome (B5)
at any positive b. A signed or operator-level stationary reduction could
avoid this absolute entropy loss; none is proved here.

## 8. Status and continuation

Completed: actual operator-telescoping trace/pair replacement (A1-A3),
m-uniform massive inverse (B1), formal connected Gevrey-1 log theorem
(B3), and exact nontrivial connected-cancellation checks (B4).

Open: a corresponding actual oscillatory integral remainder, contour and
winding gluing, entropy-compatible saddle summation, and the desired
signed comparison. No CUE implication is claimed.

A source check is in progress for large-dimension stationary-phase and
complex cluster theorems. Sources will be imported only after their
hypotheses map to this cyclic fixed-step setting; ordinary real Laplace
results and short-total-time slicing results cannot be silently used.
